column1: # Definition-layer escapes: aliases and modeled definitions.
# An alias (`rename`) maps a corpus declaration to a real upstream record of
# the same kind.  The reason says why the corpus cannot use the upstream
# spelling; the target must exist, so a rename never smuggles in a definition.
# A modeled row has no upstream ODS record.  The witness is a `path:line` that
# must (a) exist, (b) suit the category, and (c) mention the symbol quoted in
# the reason.  Categories are a closed vocabulary:
#   cxx-type       hand-written C++ type / value object; witness .h or .td
#   builtin        builtin attribute/type used as a payload; witness under
#   constraint     TableGen constraint alias, not a def;   witness .td
#   borrowed-enum  enum record owned by another dialect;   witness outside
# A modeled definition uses `Assembly Modeled;` (opaque) or a *flat spine*
# block: string literals, declared parameters and `params` only.  `Modeled;`
# declares no parameters (D12); a block is checked for the full parameter list
# (D4) and against directives/control flow (D11).  A row is stale if no corpus
